records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy nanomaterials be used as electrocatalysts for advanced energy conversion applications?. System: 2D high‐entropy transition metal dichalcogenides, (MoWVNbTa)S2, Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27, PGM–HEA, PdPtCuAgAu, RuFeCoNiCu, PtPdRhRuCe. Processing: chemical vapor transport method, liquid‐phase exfoliation, synthesis of uniform NPs. Test conditions: CO2 reduction at different potentials, alcohol oxidation reaction in 1.0 m KOH solution with 1.0 m ethanol, nitrogen reduction reaction, ammonia oxidation reaction. Findings: Up to −0.31 V versus RHE, the FE of CO formation was over 90%; PGM–HEA showed a much higher j specific value in comparison to single platinum group metal NPs; PdPtCuAgAu NWs showed the largest mass activity and the lowest onset potential among other Pd‐based metal nanocatalysts; RuFeCoNiCu/CP showed a low overpotential (0.05 V vs RHE) and high FE (38.5%) for NRR; PtPdRhRuCe NPs exhibited ≈100% conversion of ammonia and >99% selectivity toward nitrogen oxides. Mechanism: The enhanced catalytic activity of HENMs is explained by the cocktail effect, and the d‐band center of the alloy and the absorption energy are related to electrocatalysis. Limitations: There are still fundamental and practical issues of HENMs as electrocatalysts to be considered, such as moderate synthesis strategies, structural control, optimization of element combination and composition, and reaction mechanism. Future work: Developing an advanced synthetic approach, unveiling the relationship between the properties of HENMs and the catalytic activity, and discovery of reaction mechanisms. Quote: "Beyond metal alloys, 2D HEMs are getting attention because of their large surface area"
